ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (23) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

The parable of the vineyard (Matthew 21:33–41) is translated from Tolstoy's Russian, with «хозяин» (khozyain, 'master') kept as 'master' of the vineyard and of the garden; «разум» (razum) is 'reason' throughout. «Выковал» (vykoval, 'forged') in the parable is read as «выкопал» (vykopal, 'dug'), the Synodal wording, and flagged.
Source observation: [17] «выковал в нем точило» ('forged a winepress in it') for the Synodal «выкопал» ('dug'); evidently a one-letter slip, translated 'dug'.
Source observation: [2] «чего они желают; возможность совершенствования» has a semicolon where a colon is evidently meant before the explanation; rendered with a colon.
